problems.title: Recognise a function from a graph
problems.question: Which of the four displayed graphs represent a function of $x$?
problems.idea: A function can assign only one output to each input. Use the vertical-line test.
formulas: A graph represents $y=f(x)$ if every vertical line intersects its included points at most once.
A filled dot is included; an open circle is excluded.
steps: Graph I has a filled point above the sloping line at the same $x$-coordinate. That input has two outputs, so I fails.
Graph II has an open circle on the sloping line at $x=0$ and a filled replacement point above it. Only the filled point is included at that input; II passes.
Graph III has two filled points on the vertical axis. It fails because $x=0$ has two outputs.
Graph IV is a broken line with no vertical segment or fold back. Each input has one output, so it passes.

problems.title: The y-intercept through two points
problems.question: Find the ordinate of the point where the line through $(5,3)$ and $(2,-6)$ meets the $y$-axis.
problems.idea: Find the slope, then substitute a point to find the constant term.
steps: Substitute $(5,3)$ into $y=3x+b$: $3=15+b$.
Thus $b=-12$, and the line meets the $y$-axis at $(0,-12)$.

problems.title: A family of lines through a fixed point
problems.question: Which displayed formula describes a nonvertical line through $(2,3)$ for any choice of slope $k$?
problems.idea: The fixed point must satisfy the formula for every $k$.
steps: Expanding gives $y=kx+3-2k$.
Check: at $x=2$, the right side is $2k+3-2k=3$, whatever $k$ is.
problems.note: The vertical line $x=2$ also passes through the point, but cannot be written as $y=kx+b$ with finite $k$. The choices concern lines expressible in that form.

problems.title: Are two conditions needed?
problems.question: For $f(x)=kx+b$, condition I says $f(-2)=15$ and condition II says $f(1)=-4$. Which conditions are sufficient to determine the sign of $b$?
problems.idea: One point leaves the slope free; two distinct points determine the line.
steps: Condition I alone gives $b=15+2k$, which can be positive, zero, or negative as $k$ varies.
Condition II alone gives $b=-4-k$, which also allows all three signs.
Together: $-2k+b=15$ and $k+b=-4$. Subtract to obtain $-3k=19$, so $k=-19/3$.
problems.answer: Both conditions together are sufficient; neither alone is sufficient (option დ).

problems.title: A function relating base angles and altitude angles
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base angles $x$. Express the angle between the altitude rays pointing towards the two base vertices as a function of $x$.
problems.idea: The apex angle is $180^\circ-2x$, and the angle formed by those altitude rays is its supplement.
formulas: For the altitude intersection $H$ and base vertices $A,C$, $\angle AHC=180^\circ-B$.
steps: Name the apex $B$ and base vertices $A,C$. Since $A=C=x$, the apex angle is $180^\circ-2x$.
The altitude lines are perpendicular to $BC$ and $BA$. The angle $AHC$ formed towards the base vertices is supplementary to the apex angle.
Hence $\angle AHC=180^\circ-(180^\circ-2x)=2x$.
problems.answer: $f(x)=2x$ (option ბ), using the altitude-ray angle described above.
problems.note: The source simply says “angle between altitudes.” If it instead means the smaller angle between the infinite altitude lines, that value is $\min(2x,180^\circ-2x)$. The listed answer $2x$ uses the customary named altitude-ray angle.

problems.title: Equal distances from the x-axis
problems.question: For which values of $p$ are $A(p,3)$ and $B(5,p-1)$ equally distant from the $x$-axis?
problems.idea: The distance to the horizontal axis is the absolute value of the vertical coordinate.
steps: Point $A$ is $|3|=3$ units from the $x$-axis.
Point $B$ is $|p-1|$ units away, so $|p-1|=3$.
Thus $p-1=3$ or $p-1=-3$, giving $p=4$ or $p=-2$.

problems.title: Translate an entire line
problems.question: Translate the line $y=2x-5$ by sending every point $(x,y)$ to $(x-3,y+1)$. Find the new line.
problems.idea: Express the old coordinates in terms of the translated coordinates before substituting.
steps: Substitute into the original equation: $Y-1=2(X+3)-5$.
Simplify: $Y-1=2X+1$, hence $Y=2X+2$.
Rename the new coordinates $x,y$: the translated line is $y=2x+2$.

problems.title: Excluded inputs of a rational function
problems.question: For which real values of $x$ is $y=\dfrac{5x-1}{(4x^2-9)(|x|-3)}$ undefined?
problems.idea: A fraction is undefined when any denominator factor is zero.
formulas: A real fraction requires a nonzero denominator.
steps: Combine both sets. No other real input makes the denominator zero.

problems.title: A parallel line through a known point
problems.question: The lines $y=0.8x+1$ and $y=kx+b$ are parallel. The second contains $A(-1.5,-2)$. Find $k$ and $b$.
problems.idea: Parallel nonvertical lines have the same slope.
steps: The first line has slope $0.8$, so $k=0.8$.
Therefore $b=-2+1.2=-0.8$.

problems.title: A third line through an intersection
problems.question: Which listed line passes through the intersection of $y=-1.3x-0.7$ and $y=3x-5$?
problems.idea: At an intersection, the two expressions for $y$ agree. Then check that point in the choices.
formulas: For an intersection of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$, solve $f(x)=g(x)$.
steps: Substitute into $y=3x-5$: $y=-2$.
The listed line $y=0.5x-2.5$ gives $y=0.5-2.5=-2$ at $x=1$. It passes through $(1,-2)$.
The other listed formulas give $7,3,5,-3,16$ at $x=1$, so none contains the intersection.

problems.title: Parallel through the intersection of two other lines
problems.question: Line $f$ is parallel to $y=x-2.7$ and passes through the intersection of $y=-0.5x+1$ and $y=2x-6.5$. Find its $y$-intercept.
problems.idea: Find the intersection first; then use the required slope of $1$.
formulas: Parallel nonvertical lines have equal slopes.
steps: The intersection has $y=-0.5(3)+1=-0.5$.
The new line has slope $1$, so $y=x+b$.

problems.title: Read a slope and intercept from a diagram
problems.question: The displayed line decreases, crosses the $y$-axis at $2.7$, and makes an acute $45^\circ$ angle with the $x$-axis. Which equation describes it?
problems.idea: A $45^\circ$ line changes one vertical unit per horizontal unit; decreasing means the slope is negative.
formulas: A $45^\circ$ right triangle has equal legs, so the slope magnitude is $1$.
steps: The intercept is $b=2.7$.
The line slopes down to the right, so its slope is $m=-1$.
Substitute these into $y=mx+b$ to get $y=-x+2.7$.

problems.title: An angle made by intersecting chords
problems.question: Diameter $AB$ and chord $CD$ meet at $M$. Given $\angle CMB=65^\circ$ and arc $CB=110^\circ$, find minor arc $BD$.
problems.idea: An angle inside a circle is half the sum of the arcs intercepted by it and its vertical angle.
formulas: An arc with endpoints of a diameter is a semicircle of $180^\circ$.
steps: $65=\frac12(110+\widehat{AD})$.
Multiply by $2$ and subtract $110$: $\widehat{AD}=20^\circ$.
On the semicircle containing $D$, arcs $AD$ and $DB$ add to $180^\circ$.
Thus $\widehat{BD}=180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ$.

problems.title: When a linear function decreases
problems.question: For which $a$ is $y=(a-2)x-3$ a decreasing function?
problems.idea: The slope tells whether a linear function increases or decreases.
steps: The slope is $a-2$.
Require $a-2<0$, so $a<2$.
At $a=2$ the function is constant; at $a>2$ it increases.

problems.title: Test points against a shaded region
problems.question: The line $y=kx$ passes through $E(2,-1)$. The diagram shades the region above the line on the left of the $y$-axis. Which of $A(-1,-2)$, $B(-5,3)$, $C(-3,2)$ lie there?
problems.idea: Find the boundary line, then compare each point’s height with the line at the same input.
steps: Using $E$, $k=-1/2$. All three candidate points have negative $x$, so test whether $y>-x/2$.
At $A$, the boundary height is $0.5$, but $-2<0.5$: A is outside.
At $B$, the boundary height is $2.5$, and $3>2.5$: B is inside.
At $C$, the boundary height is $1.5$, and $2>1.5$: C is inside.

problems.title: Combine inscribed and tangent angles
problems.question: In the diagram, tangents from $B$ touch the circle at $C,D$ and form angle $\alpha$. Point $E$ lies on the major arc $CD$, with $\angle CED=\alpha+15^\circ$. Find $\alpha$.
problems.idea: Both angles are related to the same minor arc $CD$.
formulas: An inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc.
An angle between two tangents equals $180^\circ$ minus the minor-arc measure.
steps: The minor arc $CD$ has measure $2(\alpha+15^\circ)$.
The tangent angle therefore satisfies $\alpha=180^\circ-2(\alpha+15^\circ)$.
Expand: $\alpha=150^\circ-2\alpha$, giving $3\alpha=150^\circ$.
Thus $\alpha=50^\circ$. Check: the arc is $130^\circ$ and its supplementary tangent angle is $50^\circ$.

problems.title: The triangle formed by incircle contact points
problems.question: Triangle $ABC$ has $\angle B=80^\circ$. Join the three contact points of its incircle. Find the angle of the contact triangle whose vertex lies on $AC$.
problems.idea: The two sides through $B$ are tangents to the incircle. Relate their contact arc to an inscribed angle.
steps: Call the contact points on $AB,BC$ respectively $Q,R$, and the one on $AC$ call $P$.
The angle between tangents $BQ,BR$ is $80^\circ$, so the minor arc $QR$ facing $B$ is $180^\circ-80^\circ=100^\circ$.
Point $P$ is on the other arc. Thus $\angle QPR$ intercepts that $100^\circ$ arc.
The required angle is $100^\circ/2=50^\circ$.

problems.title: Equal chords and a diameter
problems.question: In the diagram, $EC=CD$, $\angle ECD=54^\circ$, and $BD$ is a diameter. Find $\angle BDC$.
problems.idea: Equal chords subtend equal arcs; the diameter supplies a semicircle.
formulas: An inscribed angle is half its intercepted arc.
Equal chords subtend equal minor arcs.
steps: Angle $ECD$ intercepts the arc $ED$ not containing $C$, which measures $2\cdot54^\circ=108^\circ$.
The remaining two arcs $EC$ and $CD$ are equal. Each is $(360^\circ-108^\circ)/2=126^\circ$.
In the displayed order, $B$ lies on arc $EC$ and arc $BCD$ is a semicircle. Hence arc $BC=180^\circ-126^\circ=54^\circ$.
Angle $BDC$ intercepts arc $BC$, so it equals $54^\circ/2=27^\circ$.

problems.title: Chord intersection from four arc ratios
problems.question: Points $A,B,C,D$ occur in that order on a circle, with consecutive arcs in ratio $AB:BC:CD:DA=3:2:2:5$. Find the smaller angle between chords $AC$ and $BD$.
problems.idea: Convert the ratio to degrees, then use the intersecting-chord angle rule.
formulas: Adjacent angles at intersecting lines add to $180^\circ$.
steps: The ratio totals $12$ parts, so one part is $360^\circ/12=30^\circ$.
The arcs are $90^\circ,60^\circ,60^\circ,150^\circ$.
Thus $\angle APB=(90^\circ+60^\circ)/2=75^\circ$.
The adjacent angle is $180^\circ-75^\circ=105^\circ$, so the smaller angle is $75^\circ$.

problems.title: A tangent, a central secant, and an arc
problems.question: In the diagram, $MK$ is tangent at $K$, and secant $MCB$ passes through the centre $O$. If $\angle KMB=35^\circ$, find minor arc $KC$.
problems.idea: The radius to a tangent contact makes a right triangle.
formulas: Arc measure equals the corresponding central angle.
steps: Triangle $MOK$ is right-angled at $K$, with angle $35^\circ$ at $M$.
So $\angle MOK=180^\circ-90^\circ-35^\circ=55^\circ$.
Rays $OM$ and $OC$ coincide, so $\angle KOC=55^\circ$.
The minor arc $KC$ has the same measure.

problems.title: Where can a circle’s centre be?
problems.question: Two distinct points are fixed in a plane. What figure is formed by the centres of all circles through both points?
problems.idea: A circle’s centre must be equally distant from its two fixed points.
formulas: The locus of points equidistant from distinct points $A,B$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.
steps: Any circle through $A,B$ has centre $O$ with $OA=OB$, both equal to its radius.
Therefore every possible centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.
Conversely, any point on that perpendicular bisector has equal positive distances to $A$ and $B$, so it is the centre of a circle through them.
The complete locus is the whole perpendicular-bisector line.

problems.title: A 30-degree angle subtending a chord
problems.question: Points $A,B,C,D$ lie on a circle. Diameter $AB$ is $20$ cm and $\angle CDA=30^\circ$. Find $AC$.
problems.idea: Use the inscribed-angle rule and the right triangle on a diameter.
formulas: Angles subtending the same chord are equal or supplementary, depending on their arcs.
An angle on a diameter is $90^\circ$.
In a right triangle, the side opposite $30^\circ$ is half the hypotenuse.
steps: Chord $CA$ is subtended by angle $CDA=30^\circ$. The angle $CBA$ is therefore $30^\circ$ or $150^\circ$.
Because $AB$ is a diameter, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$. Thus $\angle CBA$ must be acute; it is $30^\circ$.
In right triangle $ABC$, side $AC$ lies opposite $30^\circ$, with hypotenuse $AB=20$ cm.
Hence $AC=20/2=10$ cm.

problems.title: Tangents when the given arc is major
problems.question: An arc $BC$ measures $210^\circ$. Find the smaller angle between the two tangent rays meeting outside the circle at their common point.
problems.idea: First convert the major arc to the complementary minor arc.
steps: The minor arc is $360^\circ-210^\circ=150^\circ$.
The angle between the tangents towards their contact points is $180^\circ-150^\circ=30^\circ$.

problems.title: Two perpendicular projections in a right triangle
problems.question: In right triangle $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle B=30^\circ$, and $BC=10$ cm. Let $CD\perp AB$ and $DE\perp BC$. Find $BE$.
problems.idea: Use the 30-degree rule in triangle $BCD$, then similarity for the second projection.
formulas: In a right triangle, the side opposite $30^\circ$ is half the hypotenuse.
Similarity of $\triangle BDE$ and $\triangle BCD$ gives $BE/BD=BD/BC$.
steps: Triangle $BCD$ is right-angled at $D$; its hypotenuse is $BC=10$ and angle at $B$ is $30^\circ$. Thus $CD=5$.
Pythagoras gives $BD^2=10^2-5^2=75$.
Triangles $BDE$ and $BCD$ share angle $B$ and are both right triangles, so they are similar.
From $BE/BD=BD/BC$, obtain $BE=BD^2/BC=75/10=7.5$ cm.

problems.title: A parameter from the height of an intersection
problems.question: The lines $y=3x+2a$ and $y=2x+6-a$ intersect at a point with ordinate $11$. Find $a$.
problems.idea: At their intersection, substitute the same $x$ and the given $y=11$ into both equations.
formulas: An intersection point satisfies both line equations simultaneously.
steps: The equations become $3x+2a=11$ and $2x-a=5$.
From the second, $a=2x-5$.
Substitute into the first: $3x+2(2x-5)=11$, so $7x=21$ and $x=3$.
Then $a=2(3)-5=1$. Both line formulas give $y=11$ at $x=3$.
